facts.name: Calendula
facts.color: Orange or yellow, sometimes cream (orange shown)
facts.light: Full sun to part sun; well-drained soil
facts.notes: Also called pot marigold (not a true marigold). Bright orange or yellow daisies from early summer until a hard frost; bees and butterflies visit. An annual that likes cool weather: it may slow down in midsummer heat and picks up again when it cools. Snip off faded flowers to keep it blooming.

sources.title: MIgardener (Michigan seed company): Calendula, Pacific Beauty Mix
sources.note: Calendula officinalis seed sold by a Michigan company with a store in St. Clair, MI.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Calendula
sources.note: 12 to 24 inches by variety; orange, yellow, white and bicolor flowers that bloom almost nonstop until the first heavy frost. May slow in hot weather and recover when it cools. Full sun, well-drained soil, little fertilizer; deadhead for more flowers. Reseeds, but not aggressively. Watch for aphids and powdery mildew.

sources.title: Gardenia: Calendula officinalis (Pot Marigold)
sources.note: 1 to 2 ft tall and wide; full sun or part sun. If flowering fades in midsummer, cut it back hard.

sources.title: Rutgers NJAES: Landscape Plants Rated by Deer Resistance (printable list)
sources.note: Annuals: calendula and strawflower are rated A (rarely damaged); California poppy, verbena and zinnia B (seldom severely damaged); cosmos C (occasionally severely damaged).

companions.why: Recommended companions for pot marigold include lavender and zinnias.
